data.content_ref: inline:Relation Kind: Reduction of Normativity to Description. The isolated context reduces to the neighbourhood; the apparent 'decision' to prefer theories is nothing more than a descriptive label for the psychological and sociological effects of evolutionary selection on scientists, eliminating the normative layer entirely. REFUTED IF: Scientists can and do consciously violate the evolutionary imperative (e.g., clinging to falsified theories despite social pressure), proving the decision is a distinct normative act not reducible to description.
